title: Region selection system: box/ellipse/magic-wand, PS modifiers, region-targeted fill, ⌘N new layer
goal: USER (2026-07-04, verbatim intent): Photoshop-style REGION selection — box select, circle select, magic wand, snap to edges, ⇧/⌥ modifiers to add/remove — and region-targeted operations: fill the selected area; ⌘N creates a new (empty) layer WITHOUT resetting the selection so you can fill on it. Region selection is distinct from layer selection (the arrow tool) and SUPERSEDES layers by default: while a region exists, ops (fill, delete, copy) target the region. This replaces/extends today's rect-only marquee (EditorState.selection: CGRect).

designNotes.model: Selection becomes a PATH-based region, not a CGRect. Core type SelectionRegion wrapping CGPath (CoreGraphics-only, OK for PhotonzCore; it is EDITOR state, not document state — no Codable needed, lives on EditorState like the current rect). Booleans via the macOS 13+ CGPath.union/subtracting/intersection(using:) APIs — VERIFY these behave on macOS 26 before building on them (spike first). Rect/ellipse builders; bounds accessor (existing consumers need a rect); contains(point). Magic wand output (a bitmap mask from flood fill) converts to CGPath via a marching-squares contour tracer (core, TDD) so EVERYTHING stays path-based and ants/fill/booleans are uniform.
designNotes.wand: Flood fill from the click point over the COMPOSITE bitmap (what the user sees), tolerance option (Euclidean RGB distance), contiguous-only v1. Runs off-main like the edge map (Task.detached; cache not needed — one-shot per click). Render-side helper in PhotonzRender (needs bitmaps), TDD with synthetic fixtures.
designNotes.toolsAndModifiers: New tools: rect-select, ellipse-select, magic wand. The CURRENT select tool (arrow) stays layer selection. Today's plain-drag marquee on the arrow tool should keep working (it IS rect-select in practice — decide whether arrow-drag delegates to the new region system; recommended: yes, one selection model everywhere). Modifiers at gesture start: ⇧ add, ⌥ subtract, ⇧⌥ intersect. SHORTCUT CONFLICTS to resolve with the user: PS uses M/W but M=measure here; candidates: S (rect select), ⇧S cycle to ellipse, W (wand) — W is free.
designNotes.snapping: Marquee corners magnetize to the EdgeMap exactly like measure corners (EdgeSnapping, windowed queries, ⌘ bypass). The edge map is currently GATED to the measure tool (EditorState.measureEdgeMap) — widen the gate to selection tools.
designNotes.regionSupersedesLayer: While a region exists: bucket/⌥⌫ fill paints the region (clipped path) INTO the target layer's pixels — for image layers bake into a copy of the bitmap (destructive-but-undoable, like merge); ⌫ erases region pixels to transparent on the selected image layer; ⌘C copies the region from the composite (exists for rects — generalize to path with clip). Existing consumers of selection:CGRect to migrate: promoteSelectionToLayer/⌘J, blurBehindSelection, copy, Document.layerIDs(fullyInside:) (use region bounds), CanvasView ants (CAShapeLayer takes any CGPath — swap paths; marching-ants crawl animation unchanged).
designNotes.cmdN: NEW EMPTY LAYER command (canvas-sized transparent image layer), selection PRESERVED (it is EditorState state — simply do not clear it on layer add; audit setSelection(nil) call sites). SHORTCUT = OPEN DECISION, ask the user before wiring (discussed 2026-07-04, no answer yet): Photoshop uses ⌘N for New DOCUMENT, ⇧⌘N for New Layer (with dialog), ⌥⇧⌘N instant. Option A (user's original ask): ⌘N = new layer; move New from Clipboard to ⌥⌘N. Option B (PS parity): keep ⌘N = New from Clipboard, ⇧⌘N = instant new layer; move New Window (current ⇧⌘N) to ⌥⌘N.
designNotes.fillOnNewLayer: The user's flow: make a selection → ⌘N → bucket/⌥⌫ → the fill lands on the fresh transparent layer clipped to the region, selection still active for further ops. Empty image layer = registered transparent bitmap (or a lighter 'empty' content? simplest: canvas-sized transparent CGImage, but that is 4·W·H bytes — consider a lazy/solid-clear ImageStore entry or bake-on-first-fill instead of materializing upfront).
designNotes.priorArt: Read first: EditorState.selection/setSelection + Marquee.swift (current rect model), CanvasView selectionBase/AntsLayer + MarqueeDrag, EdgeSnapping/EdgeMap (16.4/16.5), Fill.swift + fillLayer (16.11), rasterize(region:) (merge-down / ⌘C paths).

tasks.title: Core SelectionRegion: path model, rect/ellipse builders, booleans, bounds/contains (TDD) + CGPath-boolean spike
tasks.notes: SPIKE PASSED (2026-07-05): CGPath.union/subtracting/intersection all correct on macOS 26 — rects, ellipses, disjoint, holes, 20 chained ops; empty results come back isEmpty=true with null bbox. Built Sources/PhotonzCore/SelectionRegion.swift: init?(path) collapses no-area paths to nil, rect/ellipse builders, Mode{replace,add,subtract,intersect} + Mode(shift:option:) modifier mapping, combining(_:mode:), static combine(base?:with:mode:) (nil base: replace/add→shape, subtract/intersect→nil), bounds, contains (even-odd everywhere). @unchecked Sendable with comment (CGPath immutable copy at init; CGPath itself unmarked because CGMutablePath subclasses it). 17 tests in SelectionRegionTests.swift; 602 total green.

tasks.title: Marching-squares contour tracer: bitmap mask → CGPath (core, TDD)
tasks.notes: Sources/PhotonzCore/ContourTracer.swift: ContourTracer.path(fromMask:[Bool],width:,height:) -> CGPath?. Grid-edge tracing (not classic per-cell marching squares): each filled pixel emits directed clockwise edges on empty-facing sides, keyed (vertex*4+dir) — unique by construction; loops chained with right-turn-first at saddles so diagonal blobs stay separate contours; collinear runs merged (corners only). Pixel (x,y) covers unit square (x,y)-(x+1,y+1), top-left origin, even-odd like SelectionRegion. nil on empty/mis-sized mask. 11 tests (single px, full frame, two blobs, donut, ring+island=3 subpaths, diagonal, L-shape, SelectionRegion round-trip + boolean). 613 green.

tasks.title: Magic wand flood fill (render, TDD): composite sample + tolerance
tasks.notes: Sources/PhotonzRender/FloodFill.swift: FloodFill.mask(in: CGImage, from: CGPoint, tolerance:) -> Mask{[Bool],w,h}? + path(...) -> CGPath? convenience (mask → ContourTracer). Scanline fill, 4-connected; tolerance = Euclidean RGBA distance in 0–255 units vs the SEED pixel (PS semantics — no gradient creep; alpha included so transparent/opaque black differ). Decodes via CGContext RGBA8 top-left row order (same as EdgeMapAnalyzer). nil on out-of-bounds seed. 11 tests (boundaries, contiguity incl. diagonal no-leak, concave U, tolerance thresholds √(3·4²), seed-not-neighbor gradient, path round-trip). 624 green. Still TODO app-side: run off-main on wand click (composite can be 12MP).

tasks.title: Selection tools on canvas: rect/ellipse/wand + ⇧/⌥/⇧⌥ modifiers + edge snapping + ants (app)
tasks.notes: Tool gains rectSelect/ellipseSelect/wand + isRegionSelectionTool + preservesSelectionRegion (region survives switches within select family + fill; cleared for drawing/crop/text — tested). EditorState.selection is now SelectionRegion?; setSelection(region, captureLayers:) — arrow marquee still rubber-band-captures layers (true), region tools pass false. wandSelect(at:mode:) renders composite + FloodFill off-main (Task.detached, fresh DocumentRenderer), drops result if canvasSize changed; wandTolerance=32 (UI in 17.6). measureEdgeMap RENAMED snappingEdgeMap, gate widened to rectSelect/ellipseSelect. CanvasView: regionDrag state (mode latched at mousedown from ⇧/⌥), EdgeSnapping on anchor + dragged corner w/ spans + ⌘ bypass like measure, live ants = combine(base, shape, mode) as ONE path via doc→view affine (view is flipped; no y-inversion), Esc cancels drag; click w/ replace mode deselects, with modifier = no-op (PS). Arrow marquee commits SelectionRegion.rect. Rect consumers (promote/blur-behind/copy/crop-seed/layerIDs(fullyInside:)) use Geometry.pixelAligned(region.bounds) — path-clipped versions land in 17.5. Toolbar: rectangle.dashed / circle.dashed / wand.and.rays after Select; only wand has a key (W) — S/M taken; OPEN: letter keys for rect/ellipse select (ask user). 626 tests green.

tasks.title: Region-targeted ops: fill/erase/copy/promote on the region; ⌘N empty layer preserving selection
tasks.notes: KEY DESIGN: EditorState.selectionTargetsPixels distinguishes region-tool selections (pixel semantics) from arrow-marquee selections (layer semantics — rubber-band capture + batch ⌫ delete, the user's primary workflow, PRESERVED). RegionOps (render, 8 tests): filled/erased/extracted with even-odd path clip, top-left coords flipped once. bakeRegion maps doc→bitmap px via layer frame; refuses cropped/transformed layers (regionTargetID only offers bakeable image layers: hit → selected → locked Background intersecting region). Bucket with pixel region fills THE REGION (click outside = no-op, PS); ⌥⌫ fills region; ⌫ erases (locked Background → BG-color fill, PS delete-on-Background); ⌘C copies path-clipped composite (supersedes selected layer); ⌘J promotes path-clipped (transparent outside blob) and consumes selection like PS Layer-via-Copy. newEmptyLayer(): canvas-sized transparent bitmap (48MB@12MP — lazy variant deferred), added on top + selected, region preserved (flow: select → New Layer → bucket). Layer▸New Layer menu item, NO shortcut yet — ⌘N decision still open with user. 634 tests green; app smoke-launched clean. Interactive verify pending user.

tasks.title: Move region content (select tool) / outline (marquee tools) — PS Move-tool semantics
tasks.notes: USER QUESTION 2026-07-05 ('move the selection of content within the current layer — how does PS do it?'), answered with PS semantics and built: SELECT (V) drag starting inside a pixel region lifts the region's pixels off the bakeable target layer (regionTargetID) — hole behind is transparent, or BG color on the locked Background (PS Move-from-Background); content floats via the EXISTING DragPreview sprite machinery (EditorState.regionMove holds extracted+holed bitmaps; underlay = composite w/ temp holed ref, removed after render; canvas regionContentDrag drives previewedFrame from the CONTENT frame, not the layer frame; regionMoveHoldFrame = post-commit no-flash hold, cleared when dragPreview clears). ⌥-drag floats a COPY (no hole). Mouse-up bakes ONE undo step via RegionOps.stamped (new: source-over at top-left rect, TDD ×3) and the selection outline FOLLOWS the content (SelectionRegion.translated, core TDD ×2). Esc/zero-delta cancels — document untouched. MARQUEE tools: plain drag inside the region moves the PIXELS too (user 2026-07-05: 'makes no sense to move the selection box only by default' — deliberate PS deviation); ⌘-drag (or an unbakeable target) moves the OUTLINE only; ⇧/⌥ drags still combine. Deltas rounded to whole px. Wand keeps click-to-select (PS outline-drag deviation, noted). Follow-ups if user wants: arrow-key nudge of region content; move cursor over region. 639 tests green.

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-06): in-app self-update — background check, menu-bar dot badge, one-click Update & Restart (no GitHub trip, no manual reinstall)
tasks.notes: USER: 'auto updating to reveal when a new version is available (glyph dot overlay in the status bar icon)' then 'I don't want to go to github to update, i just want it to update and restart' / 'I should never have to reinstall'. BUILT: (core, TDD ×9) CodesignInfo parse of codesign -dvv output (prefix-anchored so Authority lines can't spoof) + SelfUpdatePolicy verdict (bundle-id must match; download must have a real TeamIdentifier; when the RUNNING build has a team it must match — dev/adhoc builds pin nothing but still require a properly-signed download). (app) SelfUpdater: download versioned DMG (releases/download/vX.Y.Z/Photonz.dmg — stable per-version URL, no races with latest), hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly, verify codesign --verify --deep --strict + spctl --assess (notarization) + policy, ditto to staging, xattr -dr quarantine, detach, TRASH old bundle (recoverable; running process keeps its inode) + move staged into place; sideways-rename fallback when Trash fails. AppCoordinator: availableUpdate/updateStatus observable; startUpdateChecks() at launch +10s then every 6h (SKIPPED for dev builds — 0.0.0 would badge forever); installAvailableUpdate() → swap → pendingRelaunchBundlePath + NSApp.terminate; AppDelegate.applicationWillTerminate spawns 'sleep 0.5; open <bundle>' ONLY when the flag is set, and the flag is CLEARED on both quit-cancel paths (alert Cancel + review-not-resolved) so a later unrelated Quit can't fire a stale relaunch. UI: MenuBarIcon.image(updateAvailable:) hand-draws the dot into a template NSImage (SwiftUI overlays flatten unreliably in MenuBarExtra) with a punched gap; menu gains 'Update to vX.Y.Z & Restart' (label becomes the live phase while installing); Check for Updates… alert now offers Update & Restart (Download… fallback for dev builds). VERIFIED: real SelfUpdater run against a scratch dist copy restamped 0.3.0 → downloaded published v0.4.0, all checks passed, bundle became notarized 0.4.0 (spctl accepted, team VMGW2V57S7), old copy trashed; badge icon rendered to PNG (dot + gap reads clearly); 670 tests green. NOTE: users must install ONE more release manually — self-update only exists in builds that contain it.

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-19): Load layer pixels as a selection — ⌘-click a layer row (PS load-transparency)
tasks.notes: USER: 'when i ctrl click a layer, i'd like it to select the pixels in the layer.' Clarified (ctrl-click already opens the 17.12 context menu): ⌘-click (PS parity) on the Layers panel ROW. BUILT: (render, TDD ×4) DocumentRenderer.layerSelectionPath(for:in:store:alphaThreshold:) in LayerSelectionMask.swift — renders the layer ALONE at full opacity with soft effects stripped (shadow/blur/opacity removed so the selection hugs the shape not its glow; border + corner radius KEPT as visible shape), reads RGBA, thresholds alpha≥128 to a mask, traces to a canvas-space even-odd CGPath via existing ContourTracer (17.2). Footprint = transformed frame corners clamped to canvas, .integral so the path lines up 1:1 with pixels. nil when nothing opaque. Tests: filled rect silhouette (bounds + interior/exterior contains), soft effects don't bleed/empty, solid image → full frame, transparent → nil. (app) EditorState.selectLayerPixels(id:) → SelectionRegion(path) + setSelection(region, captureLayers:false) = PIXEL-targeting selection (fill/copy/delete/promote target it), layer stays selected, no-op if nothing opaque. (UI) LayersPanel row .highPriorityGesture(TapGesture().modifiers(.command)) loads pixels (plain tap still selects); 'Select Pixels' context-menu item for discovery. NOTE for outline-only shapes: selects the stroke ring (even-odd hole) — literally 'the pixels', PS-accurate. 721 tests green; dev bundle relaunched. PENDING user verify: ⌘-click shape row → ants around shape; fill/copy targets it.

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-19): Rasterize Layer — bake a vector shape/annotation layer into committed pixels (right-click)
tasks.notes: USER: right-click a shape layer → 'Rasterize Layer' converts it to pixel content; render the shape as it currently appears (fully flattened) into a bitmap, store in ImageStore, replace LayerContent with .image(ImageRef). Bake everything in (decided w/ user): all non-destructive LayerStyle effects (blur/shadow/border/corner radius/opacity) + geometry (crop/transform) flattened into pixels, then RESET style to default. BUILT: (core, TDD ×4) Layer.isRasterizable (annotation content ONLY — text/measure/zoomCallout/collage draw chrome outside the frame or carry semantics a lone bitmap can't reproduce; image already pixels) + PhotonzDocument.rasterizeLayer(id:rasterized:frame:) swaps content→.image, resets style/crop/transform, keeps id/name/slot/visibility/lock. KEY DECISION: blend mode is RELATIONAL (composites vs layers below) so it can't be baked into an isolated bitmap — the layer's effectiveBlendMode is carried onto the image layer (rasterized highlight keeps multiplying → stays pixel-identical). (render, TDD ×1) RasterizeLayerRenderTests: styled rect (opacity+rounded+border+shadow) composite before/after is pixel-stable (max Δ≤12, <2% channels drift >6). (app) EditorState.rasterizeLayer(id:) mirrors mergeLayers for ONE participant: padded transformed-bounds footprint clamped to canvas, composites ONLY that layer via existing DocumentRenderer.rasterize(region:) (reuses the single coord flip — no hand-rolled flip), registers bitmap, applies core mutation through History.perform (undo restores the vector). canRasterizeLayer(id:) gates. Wired into LayersPanel row context menu (shown only when rasterizable) + Layer menu (disabled otherwise). 717 tests green; dev bundle built + launched. PENDING user verify: right-click shape → Rasterize Layer looks identical + undo brings back editable vector.

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-18): responsive editor layout — no clip/push-off at small window sizes (toolbar overflow menu, inspector auto-collapse, layers list scroll, sensible window floor)
tasks.notes: USER: editor UI broke when the window was smaller than the ideal layout — right inspector pushed fully OFF-SCREEN, floating toolbar tools clipped at both window edges, layers list truncated silently past ~8 layers, no strategy for constrained sizes. REPRO (TCC blocks live screenshots from this terminal — no Screen Recording/Automation grant): built an offscreen ImageRenderer harness mirroring EditorView's exact composition (HStack{ ZStack{canvas; wide floating toolbar} ; fixed-width inspector }); at the OLD 760×520 floor the inspector labels already clipped ('Laye/Effe/Sha') and the toolbar's leading tools were cut off; at 500×400 the panel was entirely gone. ROOT CAUSE: the ~850pt floating toolbar has a large intrinsic min width that props the canvas ZStack open, and the fixed-width inspector in the HStack has nothing to yield, so the pair overflows the window and the panel is pushed past the right edge; the toolbar itself never overflowed, it just clipped. FIX: (core, TDD) Sources/PhotonzCore/EditorChromeLayout.swift — pure policy: minWindowWidth 480 / minWindowHeight 400 (low floor so responsive kicks in ABOVE it), inspectorAutoCollapseWidth 680 + shouldAutoCollapseInspector(windowWidth:), and visibleItemCount(available:itemWidths:spacing:overflowWidth:) greedy fit that reserves a trailing overflow control; 12 tests. (app) PhotonzApp scene frame uses the core min constants (was hard-coded 760×520). EditorView: body wrapped in GeometryReader; the tool row measures its fixed neighbors (color+zoom group via ToolbarSideWidthKey, contextual wand/crop/style segments via ToolbarContextWidthKey) and, when the full set won't fit, collapses trailing tools behind an 'ellipsis' overflow Menu (ToolbarSlot enum drives order + menu rows; the ACTIVE tool is never overflowed). When everything fits it renders the ORIGINAL toolsBar unchanged → zero regression at large sizes. Inspector auto-collapses below 680 (remembers whether WE hid it vs the user, restores on widen) with an in-window sidebar toggle (top-trailing glass button, sidebar.trailing/leading) as the reveal affordance; canvas keeps priority so the panel never pushes off. LayersPanel: listHeight no longer caps at 320 (that + scrollDisabled truncated the stack); it grows to fit all rows so the single outer inspector ScrollView scrolls everything, one axis, no nested-scroll jank. VERIFIED: 715 tests green (incl. new EditorChromeLayout suite); harness re-rendered against the FIXED structure at 1100/820/620/500 — inspector fully on-screen when shown, toolbar collapses to '…' with color+zoom intact and nothing at the window edge, panel auto-collapses + reveal button appears when narrow; real app bundle rebuilt, relaunched with a photo, runs idle at 0% CPU (no preference-key feedback loop). The 'You're running a debug build…' banner in the user's shot is a macOS system notice, not Photonz chrome — outside our code, but the min-size floor now guarantees the window has room for it. CORRECTION (2026-07-18, after user live-tested the first cut): the estimate-based visibleItemCount UNDER-counted real widths (marquee chevron, glass padding, in-row divider) so it still clipped AND the full toolbar's intrinsic width still pushed the panel off; a ViewThatFits rewrite then CRASHED (stack overflow / AttributeGraph recursion — ViewThatFits renders every candidate and doing so with GlassEffectContainer's 9 glass variants recurses to death). FINAL: (1) the toolbar is now an .overlay(alignment:.bottom) on the canvas (an overlay does NOT add to its host's min width, so it can never push the inspector off — push-off fixed STRUCTURALLY, plus .clipped() keeps a transient over-wide bar off the panel); (2) overflow is a MEASURED feedback loop — the toolbar reports its real natural width via ToolbarContentWidthKey, the body computes the real budget from the GeometryReader, reconcileToolbarCount() steps the visible-tool count toward the largest that fits (grows only when one more tool is sure to fit, so no oscillation). Removed the dead visibleItemCount core helper + its tests; kept the auto-collapse + window-floor policy (pure, tested). 707 tests green; app rebuilt + launched with a photo, idles at 0% CPU, NO crash. PENDING user verify: live resize feel (screenshots blocked here by TCC).

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-19): fit editor window to the image on open (prefer 100% → grow window → reduce zoom only if a maxed window can't fit) + persist side-pane state and feed it into the sizing
tasks.notes: USER: opening a capture should size the window to the image on a strict priority: (1) always try 100%; (2) if the image at 100% fits the usable screen, grow the window to exactly image + side-pane + ~100px padding per canvas edge and show 100%; (3) only if even a maxed window can't hold 100%, max out and reduce zoom to fit with ~100px per side; (4) persist the side pane's width + expanded/collapsed and use it in the sizing math. BUILT (core, TDD ×11): Sources/PhotonzCore/EditorWindowFit.swift — pure EditorWindowFit.plan(imagePointSize:sidePaneWidth:maxContentSize:minContentSize:padding=100) -> Plan{contentSize, imageScale}. Unifies steps 2&3: neededW/H = image@100% + 2·pad (+pane on width); if it fits the max → scale 1, window hugs image+pad(+pane); else scale = min(canvasW/imgW, canvasH/imgH, 1) over the maxed canvas area, then the window HUGS the reduced image on both axes capped at max (binding axis lands on max, the other stays tight — so a wide-short image does NOT force a full-height window), floored at minContent. Points throughout (pixels ÷ pixelScale); caller converts scale→viewport zoom = scale/pixelScale (displayZoom = scale). GLUE (Sources/Photonz, thin): EditorState.sizeWindowToImageIfReady() computes maxContent = screen.visibleFrame − window chrome, minContent = window.contentMinSize (the SwiftUI .frame min + the hidden-title-bar's 32pt band — targeting the smaller EditorChromeLayout floor alone let the OS silently clamp wide-short windows), sets the frame top-left-anchored + clamped into visibleFrame, stores pendingOpenScale; canvasViewSizeChanged() applies that zoom centered once the real canvas size is known, then reveals the window. Fresh windows are held at alphaValue 0 from the new CanvasNSView.viewDidMoveToWindow→onWindowChange hook until sized (no open-time bounce; 0.35s safety-net reveal so an empty clipboard can't stick invisible); re-opening an image into an already-visible window animates the resize. PERSISTENCE: inspector width already @AppStorage('inspector.width'); added persisted inspectorPreferredVisible (UserDefaults 'inspector.visible', default true, didSet like wandTolerance) DISTINCT from the transient isLayersPanelVisible (which the view also drives from width auto-collapse) — explicit menu/in-window toggles route through EditorState.setInspectorVisible() which writes both; auto-collapse never touches the preference, so a fresh window reserves the pane's width correctly. Dev/release already get separate UserDefaults via distinct bundle ids (no key suffixing needed). VERIFIED in the real app (CGWindowList bounds, TCC blocks screenshots): 1728×1028 visibleFrame → small 400×300 opens 851×500 @100% with pane, or 600×500 when the persisted pref is collapsed (proves persisted state feeds sizing); large 6000×4000 → 1693×1028 (height maxed, width hugs, zoom 20.7%); wide 5000×300 → 1728×432 (width maxed, height at the 432 floor, zoom 25.5% — not full-height). 722 tests green (EditorWindowFit suite +11); app idles clean, no crash. FOLLOW-UP (same session): the inspector pane animated in on open (slowed the entrance); gated the show/hide spring off until one runloop after the first document load (EditorView.inspectorAnimationEnabled), so the opening state is instant and later toggles/auto-collapse still spring.

tasks.title: INTERJECTED (user 2026-07-19): editor windows shouldn't force-focus another Photonz window on close — behave like ordinary windows (return to the most-recently-used window/app)
tasks.notes: USER: with several editor windows, closing one jumped focus to another Photonz window even when they'd been in another app (e.g. opened an image over a browser via ⌃⇧H, closed it, expected the browser back). This is standard AppKit multi-window behavior (the app stays active and promotes its next window; nothing custom did it), so it had to be deliberately overridden. ITERATION (all verified live by the user; multi-app focus can't be reproduced headlessly — no Automation grant): (1) tracked the last non-Photonz app and activated it on close — worked but the ref was `weak` so the NSRunningApplication (not retained anywhere we control) deallocated to nil before the close; made it strong. (2) With the strong ref it returned to the app but FLASHED the sibling editor window forward first, because the yield was deferred a runloop (DispatchQueue.main.async) and landed after AppKit promoted the sibling. (3) Moved the yield into CloseGuardDelegate.windowShouldClose to run before the close — but the trace showed windowShouldClose is NOT called for these SwiftUI WindowGroup windows on a normal close (SwiftUI closes clean windows via NSWindow.close(), which skips it; only the willClose NOTIFICATION fires for every path). (4) FINAL MODEL (user's refined ask: 'return to the last window I was in, Photonz or not'): a global focus MRU in AppCoordinator — FocusToken.app(NSRunningApplication, held strongly) for non-Photonz activations (NSWorkspace.didActivateApplicationNotification) + FocusToken.editorWindow(windowNumber) for Photonz editor windows becoming main (NSWindow.didBecomeMainNotification), de-duped, most-recent-first, capped at 32, dead apps pruned. On NSWindow.willCloseNotification for an editor window (the one hook that fires for all close paths), drop the closing window then look at the most-recent REMAINING entry: if it's an app, activate() it SYNCHRONOUSLY on that same main-thread tick (beats AppKit's sibling promotion → no flash); if it's another Photonz window (or nothing), do nothing and let AppKit promote the next window (which is what we want). Handles both scenarios: opened-over-another-app closes back to that app; multiple editors close to the next-most-recent editor. Swift 6 clean (main-actor work wrapped in MainActor.assumeIsolated since observers use queue:.main); syncActivationPolicy still deferred a tick so the window has left the list. Removed the interim CloseGuardDelegate save-path yields (window.close() posts willClose, so the single observer covers dirty closes too). 722 tests green.
